meta.question: Has any stressed basin anywhere ever implemented surface intervention on a reservoir at a scale relevant to the Colorado?
meta.answer: No. Nothing purpose-built for evaporation control has ever operated above 1,000 ha. The largest operating cover of any kind is Los Angeles Reservoir at 71 ha, which is 0.2% of Lake Mead. The largest operating surface project of any kind is Dezhou Dingzhuang at 1200 ha, built for power on a flooded coal mine.
meta.china_finding: China has the largest floating-solar fleet on Earth, manufactures most of the world's geomembrane, and has seen deeper reservoir and lake drawdowns than the United States (Poyang fell from >350,000 ha to 81,400 ha in 2022). Its revealed strategy is inter-basin transfer, sediment regulation and ecological conveyance. It does not cover its reservoirs, and its flagship hydro-paired solar plant is land-based.
meta.why_this_matters: A cost model can be argued with. A global absence of deployment after seventy years of proposals, in every arid basin with the money to try, is harder to argue with. It applies to floating solar on these reservoirs exactly as it applies to covers.
meta.caveat: Absence of deployment is evidence about feasibility and priority, not proof of impossibility. Several of these technologies are young, and floating solar is scaling quickly on water bodies that do not fluctuate.

surface_interventions.name: Dezhou Dingzhuang
surface_interventions.relevance: The world's largest floating array, and NOT a water-supply reservoir: it sits on a flooded coal-mining subsidence lake with no drawdown duty.
surface_interventions.source: Huaneng Power International via trade press

surface_interventions.name: Lake Hefner
surface_interventions.result: 9% evaporation reduction over 88 days. Abandoned: film blown to the lee shore above a 13 mph wind limit, and replacing it took 6.5-8x the application rate of an experimental pond.
surface_interventions.relevance: The largest evaporation-suppression trial ever run, and it failed on wind. Mead has far greater fetch.
surface_interventions.source: Crow & Mitchell, wind effects on chemical films at Lake Hefner; ASABE

surface_interventions.name: Laguna Lake
surface_interventions.result: Lease awarded 2023, operations targeted 2026-2030. Not built.
surface_interventions.relevance: Would be the first surface project above 1,000 ha on a natural lake if built.

surface_interventions.name: Cirata Reservoir
surface_interventions.result: $100M, about $0.69/W. Evaporation reduction not measured or published.
surface_interventions.relevance: The largest floating solar on a genuine water-supply/hydro reservoir. Shallow, tropical, and without large level swings.

surface_interventions.name: Los Angeles Reservoir
surface_interventions.result: Deployed for bromate control; evaporation was a secondary benefit. Still in operation. $34.5M.
surface_interventions.relevance: The largest operating COVER of any kind on Earth, at 0.2% of Mead's area.

what_basins_did_instead.name: South-to-North Water Diversion
what_basins_did_instead.scale: Target 44.8 billion m3/yr; 53.1 billion m3 delivered to date on Eastern and Central routes
what_basins_did_instead.note: China's actual answer to shortage in the Hai, Huai and Yellow basins: move water, do not cover it.

what_basins_did_instead.name: Xiaolangdi, Yellow River
what_basins_did_instead.note: Storage is defended by managing sediment, which is the loss term that actually threatens Chinese reservoir capacity.

what_basins_did_instead.name: Tarim basin ecological conveyance
what_basins_did_instead.scale: 510 million m3 diverted in 2024; >10 billion yuan (~$1.5B) invested
what_basins_did_instead.note: In China's driest basin the intervention is conveyance and recharge, not surface treatment.

what_basins_did_instead.name: Longyangxia
what_basins_did_instead.scale: 2,700 ha of LAND adjacent to a 38,300 ha reservoir
what_basins_did_instead.note: The most-cited hydro-plus-solar hybrid in the world is land-based. The reservoir surface was available and was not used.
